qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Canadian Big Six banking oligopoly anchor with #1 domestic market share in retail deposits, mortgages, wealth management, and corporate banking. Protected by OSFI regulatory barriers, Bank Act ownership limits, and Canada's largest low-cost core deposit base (~C$500B+). Delivers persistent 14-17% multi-cycle ROE with unmatched domestic scale and pricing power. Primary erosion risks: Canadian residential mortgage credit cycle deterioration, OSFI regulatory capital increases (Domestic Stability Buffer), open banking mandates, and fintech payments disintermediation.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (REJECT). While Royal Bank of Canada is Canada's preeminent financial institution with an exceptional ~16% multi-cycle ROE, #1 domestic market share, and elite stewardship under CEO Dave McKay, as a fractional-reserve commercial deposit-taking bank it structurally fails the Munger Gate 6 peace-of-mind solvency standard. Operating at ~15-16x asset/equity leverage (C$2.0T+ assets vs ~C$139B equity) and funded by demand deposits, its solvency inherently relies on depositor confidence, wholesale liquidity, and central bank/CDIC backstops ('kindness of strangers').
qualitative.evidence: Canada's largest bank and premier banking oligopolist (#1 domestic share in retail deposits, mortgages, wealth management, and corporate banking). Demonstrates multi-cycle ROE consistently between 14-17% (5-year median GAAP ROIC 23.05%) and disciplined capital stewardship under CEO Dave McKay, highlighted by the strategic C$13.5B acquisition of HSBC Canada. However, Gate 6 structural rejection is absolute for commercial fractional-reserve deposit banks: total balance sheet liabilities exceed C$1.9T against CET1 ratio of ~13.0% and balance sheet leverage exceeding 15x. The funding model relies on short-duration demand deposits and wholesale capital market facilities to support long-duration residential mortgages and commercial credit, subjecting equity to asset-liability duration mismatch and credit cycle tail risk.
